transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
I’ve lost all interest in my jewelry work and the things I used to love, and I can’t make myself care enough to keep the shop going. It has just all become too much for me to handle.

Have you had other periods in your life when you felt this same kind of depression and loss of interest for at least two weeks, or is this the first time it has happened? Did it start after a specific stressful event?

No, I’ve never felt this way before; this is the first time I've ever experienced this kind of deep depression. It started after my husband developed severe complications from his diabetes and had to be hospitalized multiple times. I suddenly had to become his primary caregiver while still trying to run my shop, and the strain just completely overwhelmed me.

Have you had any thoughts of wanting to die or hurt yourself, or have you heard or seen things that others don’t? Also, are you still able to manage basic daily tasks like eating, bathing, and getting out of bed?

Sometimes I feel like it would be a relief if I just didn't wake up, and I've even counted the leftover pain pills in the bathroom, especially when I hear those quiet male and female voices whispering late at night that I'm failing. Getting out of bed and doing basic chores feels like I'm trying to move through molasses, and I've completely lost my appetite because everything is just so exhausting.

When you hear these voices, are they saying negative things about you or telling you to hurt yourself, or do they seem unrelated to your depression? Have you ever felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, or had racing thoughts during this time?

The voices whisper very hurtful things, telling me I'm a terrible wife and failing at everything, but they don't actually tell me to hurt myself. I've never felt unusually energetic; in fact, I feel completely drained and exhausted. While my mind races at night and keeps me awake, I just feel like I'm moving through molasses during the day.

final_diagnosis.reason: First episode of major depression with clear depressed mood/anhedonia, neurovegetative symptoms, psychomotor slowing, suicidal ideation, and mood-congruent auditory hallucinations. No history suggestive of prior episodes or mania/hypomania. Although onset followed caregiver stress, the presence of psychotic symptoms and severity support a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms rather than a stress-related adjustment reaction.
